landing.tagline: See the story in your tables.
landing.demoBannerBody: Data connectors are turned off on this device. You can still try the examples or upload files.
landing.modelTip: Models with strong coding and multimodal capabilities provide best experience with Datly.

about.aboutBody: A table can hold the answer and still hide it. The rows are in one program, the chart is in another, and the question is gone. Datly keeps the table, the question, and the chart in one project on this computer, so the line can be checked against the rows it came from.
about.aboutLocalBody: Projects, tables, and charts are saved as sessions on this machine. You can leave and come back without uploading the file.
about.aboutAskBody: The prompt at the bottom of the analysis pane turns a question into a thread: the words, the chart, and the table behind it.
about.aboutReadBody: Explore shows the plot and the grid. Reports keep the writing with the chart. Dashboard is where pinned charts collect.
about.docsIntro: How to open a project, bring in a table, ask for a chart, and read the result. Follow the sections in order the first time.
about.startBody: The left rail is the project. New project clears what is on screen and opens an empty workspace. The session you were in is still listed under Sessions, so you can come back to it.
about.startSteps: Docs opens this page. The arrow beside it collapses the rail to icons. On that thin rail, the arrow expands it again. The folder is Sessions, the database is Data, the bulb is Knowledge, and the plus adds a file.
about.workspaceBody: The middle is the analysis. Each question becomes a thread: the words you asked, the chart, and the table behind it. The prompt stays at the bottom of this area.
about.workspaceSteps: The canvas is the right side, and it appears only after you open a chart or a table. The project name sits in the top bar. Use that menu to rename the workspace.
about.loadBody: Open Data. Sample datasets is already connected. Expand it and select Stock prices, then choose Load. That table is 6,000 daily rows, from 30 September 2024 through 28 September 2026, for 12 large US companies.
about.loadSteps: The columns are date, symbol, company, sector, open, high, low, close, and volume. Prices are adjusted for splits, so a line does not jump when shares split. Technology, consumer, financials, health, energy, and industrials are all in the file. To use your own file, use the plus on the rail, or Add more data inside a thread. To reach a database, use the plus beside Data Connectors, then search the list.
about.askBody: Click the prompt at the bottom and describe the chart you want. The model menu on the left of the prompt chooses which model answers. The arrow sends the question.
about.askSteps: A useful question names the columns. For the stock table, try: show closing price by date for Apple and Microsoft. The reply lands in a thread. Ask a follow-up from the same prompt. With the canvas open, threads sit in two columns so the cards are not cut off.
about.canvasBody: Click a chart card to open it on the right. Explore, Reports, and Dashboard are on the canvas bar. Close is on that same bar, so the labels stay clear.
about.canvasSteps: Explore is the plot, with the table underneath. Curve, Step, and Points change the mark. Reports keeps the chart with writing you can edit. Dashboard is where pinned charts collect. Closing the canvas returns the threads to the full width.
about.tablesBody: In Explore, the data health card, the search field, and the grid are white so they stand out on the sage field. The grid has a line on every side.
about.tablesSteps: Search filters the rows you are looking at. Quick chart and Download CSV sit under the rows, not on top of them. Download CSV saves the table you are viewing.
about.sessionsBody: A session is one workspace: its tables, threads, charts, and reports. Sessions are stored on this computer. Open Sessions on the left to return to an earlier one.
about.sessionsSteps: The list can be sorted by recent edits, creation time, or name. New project does not delete the session you leave. Delete a session from its row when you no longer need it.
about.knowledgeBody: Knowledge is guidance for the agent: rules it should follow when it writes code or explores a table. Open the bulb on the left to read or edit them. They apply to later questions in this workspace.
about.dataHandlingText: Work stays on this computer. Connectors copy data into your local workspace. Language models receive small samples with your prompts.

knowledge.replayPromptConnector:
Reproduce the following analysis workflow on the connected source with source_id {{source_id}} (connector_id {{connector_id}}). Bind discovery and load to that source only. Do not probe other sources.

Workspace tables in this session are not the database. If analog parquet from that source is not already in the workspace, call load_skill('data-loading'), then list_data, find_data, describe_data, and probe_data scoped to that source. Then propose_data_operation and wait for me to confirm. Do not invent table keys.

Never emit DROP, DELETE, UPDATE, INSERT, TRUNCATE, ALTER, COPY, ATTACH, or GRANT against the source. Reads only.

After parquet from that source is in the workspace, follow the Abstract and Concrete steps in order, adapting column references to the loaded columns. Prefer Concrete when shapes match. It's fine if the result isn't identical — reproduce the same overall analysis.

Before making large assumptions, check whether the loaded data can actually support the workflow. If there is a major discrepancy — e.g. a required field or measure is missing, the granularity or shape is very different, or a step has no sensible equivalent on this data — pause and use ask_user so I can confirm how to proceed (or briefly explain the mismatch and your proposed adaptation) instead of guessing. Minor differences (renamed columns, extra columns) can be adapted silently.
